utterance: Hi Chloe, I'm Dr Chen. Sorry you're dealing with this — burning when you wee is really uncomfortable. Let me ask you a few things so I can work out what's going on. First: how long exactly has the burning been going on, and is it getting worse, the same, or better? And are you needing to wee more often or in a hurry?
reply: It started yesterday morning, so about a day and a half now, and it stings and burns worst right at the end. I am going constantly, about every half hour, and only a little bit comes out so I really have to rush.

utterance: The examination and your urine test fit with a bladder infection — a UTI, like you thought. Before I write a script: have you already taken anything for it, like paracetamol, cranberry or Ural? And since some infections passed on through sex can cause burning like this, would you like me to also send off a urine check for chlamydia, which is recommended for people your age?
reply: I haven't taken anything for it, but yeah, you can go ahead and check for that too just to be safe.

utterance:
Here's the plan, Chloe.

What's going on: your symptoms — burning at the end of passing urine, going every half hour, urgency, cloudy smelly urine and a low tummy ache — plus the urine test showing white cells and nitrites, mean you have a bladder infection, a simple UTI. I checked your temperature and your kidney areas at the back, and there's no sign the infection has reached your kidneys, and you're not generally unwell. So this is a straightforward one.

Treatment:
1. Nitrofurantoin 100 mg, one capsule twice a day for 5 days. Take it with food or a glass of milk — it's better absorbed and less likely to upset your stomach. Please finish all 10 capsules even if you feel fine after a day or two. It can turn your urine a bright yellow-orange colour, which is harmless.
2. Paracetamol 1 or 2 tablets when you need it for the pain, up to four times a day (no more than 8 tablets in 24 hours).
3. Drink plenty of water, don't hold on when you need to go, and cut back on coffee, tea and alcohol for the next few days because they irritate the bladder. You should start feeling noticeably better within 24 to 48 hours.

A couple of things worth knowing:
- If you get vomiting or diarrhoea while on the antibiotic, your pill may not be absorbed properly, so use condoms for 7 days afterwards. Otherwise, no extra contraception is needed.
- Sex probably set this off — it's very common. It's sensible to avoid sex while you're sore, and passing urine after sex afterwards may reduce the chance of it happening again.

I've also sent off the chlamydia and gonorrhoea urine test you agreed to. That takes a couple of days — the clinic will contact you with the result, and if anything comes back positive we'll treat you and let you know that your boyfriend needs treatment too.

When to get help urgently — come back to me, or go to an after-hours service or the emergency department, if you develop: a fever or shivers/rigors, pain in your back or side under the ribs, vomiting or being unable to keep the tablets down, visible blood in the urine, or you feel systemically unwell. Those can mean the infection has moved up to the kidney and needs different, stronger treatment.

Also come back if you're not clearly improving after 48 hours, or if symptoms are still there at the end of the 5 days. In that case I'd send a urine sample to the lab for culture so we can pick the right antibiotic.

Lastly, one UTI every couple of years is normal and nothing to worry about. If you find you're getting them often — say three or more a year, or every time after sex — make an appointment and we can talk about prevention options. Any questions about any of that?
reply: I don't know the word rigors, what does that mean?

utterance:
Sorry — jargon! "Rigors" just means a proper shaking, shivering attack: you feel very cold and you can't stop shaking, often with a high temperature, like a bad bout of the flu. That's different from just feeling a bit chilly. If that happens, along with pain in your back or side or being sick, it can mean the infection has travelled up to a kidney — so get seen the same day.

Otherwise, everything else the same: finish the 5 days of nitrofurantoin with food, paracetamol for the sting, plenty of water, and come back if you're not clearly better in 48 hours. We'll ring you with the chlamydia result in a couple of days. Does that all make sense, and is there anything else you'd like to ask me?
reply: No, that all makes sense, I just want to get my script so I can get back to work.

utterance: You're all set — the nitrofurantoin, the paracetamol and the urine test are all through. Take the first capsule with some food, and I hope you're feeling much better by tomorrow. Ring the clinic if anything worries you. Take care, Chloe.
reply: Thank you, I will do that. Bye.
